subject: chemistry
title: Metallic bonding and properties of metals
key_idea: A metal is a giant structure of positive metal ions in a regular pattern, surrounded by delocalised electrons. The strong attraction between the ions and the electrons gives high melting points. The moving electrons let metals conduct, and the layers can slide so metals can be shaped.

blocks.text: Metals have their own type of bonding. This section covers the structure and the metallic bond.

items.meaning: Outer-shell electrons that are not held by one atom and are free to move through the whole structure.
The strong attraction between positive metal ions and the delocalised electrons.

items: Metals have giant structures of atoms in a regular pattern, in layers.
The outer-shell electrons of each atom are delocalised.
This leaves positive metal ions, surrounded by a sea of delocalised electrons.
The sharing of the delocalised electrons gives strong metallic bonds.
A metal is positive ions in a regular pattern in a sea of delocalised electrons.
Metallic bonding is the strong attraction between the ions and the electrons.

blocks.text: Each property of a metal comes from its structure and bonding. This section explains four of them.

items: There are strong forces of attraction between the metal ions and the delocalised electrons.
A lot of energy is needed to overcome these forces, so most metals have high melting and boiling points.
The delocalised electrons can move through the metal.
They carry electrical charge through the metal, so metals conduct electricity, even as solids.
They also transfer energy, so metals conduct thermal energy.
More delocalised electrons per atom means better conduction: aluminium conducts better than sodium.
In a pure metal the atoms are arranged in layers.
The layers of metal ions can slide over each other, so the metal can be bent and shaped without breaking.
Pure metals are often too soft for many uses, so they are mixed with other metals to make alloys, which are harder.

diagram.prompt: Which type of substance has this property? Sort each one.

items: High melting point: strong attraction between metal ions and delocalised electrons.
Conductor: delocalised electrons move and carry charge or transfer energy.
Malleable: the layers of ions slide over each other.

blocks.text: Metals and non-metals can be told apart by their physical properties. This section gives the usual pattern.

items: Other metal properties are ductile (can be drawn into wires), strong and sonorous (ring when struck).
Metals form positive ions, because their atoms lose electrons.
A wire is made of metal because it is a good conductor and flexible. A polymer coat is added because a polymer is an insulator.
Most metals are shiny, dense, high-melting solids and good conductors.
Most non-metals have low boiling points and are poor conductors.

checks.q: Describe the structure and bonding in a metal.
checks.a: Positive metal ions in a regular arrangement, surrounded by a sea of delocalised electrons, with strong forces of attraction between the ions and the electrons.

checks.q: Explain why metals can be hammered into shape without breaking.
checks.a: The layers of metal ions can slide over each other.

checks.q: Explain why metals conduct electricity when solid.
checks.a: They contain delocalised electrons that can move through the metal and carry charge.

worked_example.question: Aluminium is a metal. Describe how metals conduct electricity. Answer in terms of electrons.
answer_points: Metals contain delocalised electrons, or free electrons.
The electrons move through the metal.
worked_example.tip: One mark each. Write charge, not current.

worked_example.question: Metals have high melting points. Explain, in terms of their structure and bonding, why metals have high melting points.
answer_points: Metal ions (cations) are surrounded by delocalised electrons.
There are strong forces of attraction between the delocalised electrons and the metal ions.
Lots of energy is needed to separate the particles or overcome the forces of attraction.
worked_example.tip: Any two of these points score one mark each. Do not mention covalent bonding or molecules.

worked_example.question: Describe the structure and bonding in a metal. You can include a labelled diagram in your answer.
answer_points: Positive metal ions, close packed in a regular arrangement.
The ions are surrounded by a sea of electrons.
There are strong forces of attraction between the ions and the electrons.
worked_example.tip: A diagram needs positive ions with at least one labelled electron between them. Any reference to ionic or covalent bonding scores zero.
